rules.sentence: The most common adverse event of menstrual suppression in all patient populations is breakthrough bleeding at unexpected times.
This bleeding is benign, though it can be distressing or inconvenient and is a common reason for treatment discontinuation.
Up to 46% of individuals may experience breakthrough bleeding across methods, most commonly with the subdermal etonogestrel implant and progestin-only pills.

Clinicians should counsel patients regarding possible benign breakthrough bleeding, and rates decrease with a longer duration of continuous hormonal contraceptive use, particularly if used more than 6 months.
